notes: Pass 1 (Path Traversal, CWE-022/023/036/073) LLM candidate labeling over 34 candidates (12 sources.csv rows + 22 sinks.csv rows) from iris/extraction/, all processed, none skipped.

Labeling performed in-context by the analysis LLM itself (glm-5.3, Claude Code CLI session) in 3 batches (12/9/13 candidates); no external LLM API calls were made; see labels_raw_pass1.json for batch composition and per-batch decisions.
All code evidence read from the real pymodbus_vuln source tree at the file/line anchors of the CSV rows; no CodeQL re-run was performed in this step (labeling only).

Ground-truth-looking artifacts in the source tree (VULNERABILITY_AUDIT_REPORT.md, path_traversal_sinks.csv, Chinese audit reports), CVE advisories and patch diffs were NOT read (independence rule); no source file, CodeQL database, Augur file or extraction CSV was modified.

No sanitizer entries were labeled: no normpath/abspath/realpath/relative_to/startswith/'..' rejection exists anywhere on the static-file path in the DB; the aiohttp route regex '{tail:[a-z0-9.]*}' is the only input filter and its effectiveness depends on external-library (aiohttp router) semantics not present in the CodeQL database - documented as a manual-review point in phase1_review.md, not asserted as a sanitizer.

Augur references loaded: references/patterns.md, references/python.md. No aiohttp framework reference exists in Augur references/ (checked); framework-specific shapes derived from repository code per WORKFLOW.md 4.2.3 fallback, as recorded in exploration/detection.json.

entries.rationale: Genuine untrusted HTTP input boundary: handle_html_static (routes GET /{tail:[a-z0-9.]*} at :172 and GET / at :173) reads the aiohttp request path - a client-controlled, percent-decoded URL path - as request.path[1:] into page, with zero in-code validation before os.path.join(self.web_path, page) (:262) -> open(file) (:264) and web.FileResponse(file) (:265). As a source boundary this is a true positive. Exploitability of the full flow depends on whether the aiohttp route regex (charset [a-z0-9.], anchored whole-path match) constrains request.path to separator-free values in the deployed aiohttp version - aiohttp is outside the CodeQL database, so this cannot be resolved from DB code and is flagged as the primary manual-review point (see phase1_review.md); the handler notably reads request.path directly instead of request.match_info['tail'].

entries.rationale: Taint-transfer step required for realistic propagation: os.path.join(self.web_path, page) folds the attacker-influenced `page` (argument index 1, from request.path[1:] via S05) into the result assigned to `file`, which is then passed unchanged to open(:264, K11) and web.FileResponse(:265, K12). The join performs no containment/normalization; its result semantics (attacker arg with no separators stays relative, but any separator or absolute/anchored value escapes the base) make it a pure taint propagator from arguments to return value. arg_index is corrected from the CSV's 0 (family convention) to 1 - the attacker-controlled position; the summary should propagate taint from any argument to the result.
